title: S020 4.1 Constructing and sending DHCP messages
parent_path: S020 4.1 Constructing and sending DHCP messages

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server with multiple network address (e.g., a multi-homed host) MAY use any of its network addresses in outgoing DHCP messages.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server with multiple network addresses MUST be prepared to to accept any of its network addresses as identifying that server in a DHCP message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To accommodate potentially incomplete network connectivity, a server MUST choose an address as a 'server identifier' that, to the best of the server's knowledge, is reachable from the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For example, if the DHCP server and the DHCP client are connected to the same subnet (i.e., the 'giaddr' field in the message from the client is zero), the server SHOULD select the IP address the server is using for communication on that subnet as the 'server identifier'.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server has received a message through a DHCP relay agent, the server SHOULD choose an address from the interface on which the message was recieved as the 'server identifier' (unless the server has other, better information on which to make its choice).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCP clients MUST use the IP address provided in the 'server identifier' option for any unicast requests to the DHCP server.
actions: use IP address from 'server identifier' option as unicast destination for all DHCP requests to server

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the options in a DHCP message extend into the 'sname' and 'file' fields, the 'option overload' option MUST appear in the 'options' field, with value 1, 2 or 3, as specified in RFC 1533.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the 'option overload' option is present in the 'options' field, the options in the 'options' field MUST be terminated by an 'end' option, and MAY contain one or more 'pad' options to fill the options field.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The options in the 'sname' and 'file' fields (if in use as indicated by the 'options overload' option) MUST begin with the first octet of the field, MUST be terminated by an 'end' option, and MUST be followed by 'pad' options to fill the remainder of the field.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Any individual option in the 'options', 'sname' and 'file' fields MUST be entirely contained in that field.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The options in the 'options' field MUST be interpreted first, so that any 'option overload' options may be interpreted.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The 'file' field MUST be interpreted next (if the 'option overload' option indicates that the 'file' field contains DHCP options), followed by the 'sname' field.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST adopt a retransmission strategy that incorporates a randomized exponential backoff algorithm to determine the delay between retransmissions.
actions: apply randomized exponential backoff algorithm to compute delay before each retransmission

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The delay between retransmissions SHOULD be chosen to allow sufficient time for replies from the server to be delivered based on the characteristics of the internetwork between the client and the server.
actions: choose retransmission delay sufficient to allow server reply delivery given internetwork characteristics

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For example, in a 10Mb/sec Ethernet internetwork, the delay before the first retransmission SHOULD be 4 seconds randomized by the value of a uniform random number chosen from the range -1 to +1.
actions: set first retransmission delay to 4 seconds randomized by uniform random value in [-1, +1]

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The delay before the next retransmission SHOULD be 8 seconds randomized by the value of a uniform number chosen from the range -1 to +1.
actions: set second retransmission delay to 8 seconds randomized by uniform random value in [-1, +1]

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The retransmission delay SHOULD be doubled with subsequent retransmissions up to a maximum of 64 seconds.
actions: double retransmission delay on each subsequent retransmission

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY provide an indication of retransmission attempts to the user as an indication of the progress of the configuration process.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A DHCP client MUST choose 'xid's in such a way as to minimize the chance of using an 'xid' identical to one used by another client.
actions: select xid to minimize probability of collision with xids used by other clients

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client that cannot receive unicast IP datagrams until its protocol software has been configured with an IP address SHOULD set the BROADCAST bit in the 'flags' field to 1 in any DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST messages that client sends.
actions: set BROADCAST bit in 'flags' field to 1 in DHCPDISCOVER and DHCPREQUEST messages

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client that can receive unicast IP datagrams before its protocol software has been configured SHOULD clear the BROADCAST bit to 0.
actions: clear BROADCAST bit in 'flags' field to 0

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server or relay agent sending or relaying a DHCP message directly to a DHCP client (i.e., not to a relay agent specified in the 'giaddr' field) SHOULD examine the BROADCAST bit in the 'flags' field.
actions: examine BROADCAST bit in 'flags' field before sending or relaying message directly to client

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If this bit is set to 1, the DHCP message SHOULD be sent as an IP broadcast using an IP broadcast address (preferably 0xffffffff) as the IP destination address and the link-layer broadcast address as the link-layer destination address.
actions: send DHCP message as IP broadcast using 0xffffffff as IP destination and link-layer broadcast as link-layer destination

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the BROADCAST bit is cleared to 0, the message SHOULD be sent as an IP unicast to the IP address specified in the 'yiaddr' field and the link-layer address specified in the 'chaddr' field.
actions: send DHCP message as IP unicast to 'yiaddr' with link-layer destination set to 'chaddr'

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If unicasting is not possible, the message MAY be sent as an IP broadcast using an IP broadcast address (preferably 0xffffffff) as the IP destination address and the link-layer broadcast address as the link-layer destination address.
actions: send DHCP message as IP broadcast to 0xffffffff with link-layer broadcast destination when unicasting is not possible
